newsitem.title: USA: Former Miami official's deal limits prison - paper.
newsitem.headline: Former Miami official's deal limits prison - paper.

text.p: Former Miami Finance Director Manohar Surana will serve no more than five years in prison for his role in a bribery scandal as long as he cooperates with federal prosecutors, The Miami Herald reported Friday.

The newspaper said it obtained a copy of Surana's plea agreement and other court documents, in which he confessed to attempting to solicit a $1.5 million bribe from a computer company seeking a city contract.

The newspaper said Surana also confessed in the documents that he "considered" soliciting money from the data processing firm ADP and from bond underwriters Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc, but did not carry out the plan. Both firms told prosecutors Surana never approached them.
Surana also told prosecutors that he asked Howard Gary, whose firm Howard Gary & Co was a Miami financial adviser, to give him a job after he retired, the newspaper said.
The Herald said Surana told Gary they could "make money from people interested in doing business with the city."
Gary was not immediately available for comment Thursday. Federal prosecutors previously said Gary co-operated in their investigation.
Surana also acknowledged in the documents that he attempted "to assemble a pot of money from which payments would be made to various public officials as needed," the newspaper said.
The U.S. Attorney's office declined to comment.

Confronted by the FBI in March 1996, Surana became a government witness and helped gather evidence against former City Manager Cesar Odio, lobbyist Jorge de Cardenas and former City Commissioner Miller Dawkins.

Odio and de Cardenas are scheduled to go to trial in May on charges of trying to collect kickbacks on a city worker's compensation contract. Dawkins pleaded guilty to a bribery charge and is scheduled to begin a 27-month prison term in June.
